A worker never stops for a full-check failure it did not cause: it commits, and the runner's gate judges it
The session takes main between reviews, so planning and fixes on main reach dispatch and validation within one review
A main-repair worker gets the runner's main-check evidence: log, exit code, revisions and isolated reruns
A pending reload or toolset update applies when the current review ends: no new review or Pi job starts first
A check that crashes before reporting test results is a broken check: never a red main with placeholder failures, never a pass
Only the candidate the engine will integrate next is started, and only it reads 'verifying'
A worker's TMPDIR is a short directory on disk, not the shared RAM disk
A task that fails the same way within minutes stops and asks, instead of rerunning
A task archived as done is done in the ledger too, and a not-runnable reason names what blocks it
A reviewer change re-reviews a held commit behind fresh candidates, once, and only when the change could alter its verdict
The crash line is the tool's own exit message, not an earlier warning that mentions an error
Budget-controller fixtures bound a hang, not the host's speed: no 2-second wall-clock limits
A maintainer repair that leaves a task unrunnable for the same reason is not repeated; the owner gets one question
A task closed on main whose set-aside must wait for a review is reported once, as closing, not each cycle
A conflict-held commit merged again by the resolver is adopted again when the session moved, and the resolver never runs for a merge the engine will refuse
A worker blocker that names another open task waits for that task, occupies nothing meanwhile, and resumes when it lands
The gate reuses a base run whose tree differs only in planning files, instead of running the base suite again
Explain full-check results from their recorded evidence, never from an absent log
Verified candidates integrate as a batch: one merged tree, one full check, their reviews side by side
Plans prefer independent tasks; a long dependency chain needs a reason
Chat status shows repository runners separately from plugin setup
A runner never commits or publishes uncommitted changes it did not make (GitHub #3)
A Touches-only rescope that adds a protected file integrates against the answered contract, or is refused plainly (GitHub #8)
Planning merge drivers survive a toolset self-update (GitHub #5)
Select and copy terminal TUI text by mouse dragging
Restore the offline gate for the picker-policy failures at 171b26b
A commit kept without its worker's report resumes that worker, not a batch or the merge resolver
A held commit whose branch the runner itself merged past is recovered by the runner, never asked of the owner as a rescope
A candidate that passed its batch lands before the runner reloads, and after an interrupted landing it lands first
A headless worker never stops to ask for approval; an interactive skill's approval step counts as given by the task contract
Installed dependencies of a tracked lockfile are linked into worker and review trees without per-runner settings
The autowork core SKILL.md has room again: detail moves to references/
A task whose last attempt failed its review is reworked once with the findings, never left silently held
Two runner tests fail only under full-check load
Task status shows Active, Mergeable, Waiting or Blocker with a detail
One interactive session writes the main checkout at a time
